name: Alien
generator: tools/docs_json.py (pins from the suite headers, categories from src/Library.cs, MCP tools from the server)
summary: Alien is a Grasshopper (Rhino 8) plugin: a node whose logic lives in a plain Python 3 or C# script file, with pins and on-node controls from a header comment. Describe a node in plain English and a model writes the script, runs it and fixes its own errors. Nodes are shareable files; AI agents drive everything through a built-in MCP server. It ships with a suite of architectural nodes and keeps what they generate in a library.
status: Working prototype for a uni mini-MBA pitch (mock business, no real sales). Phase 1 of BRIEF.md is done, plus the panel, library categories, the generated-asset library and the suite below. The online library, accounts and payments (Phases 2-3) are not built.
platforms: Rhino 8 on macOS (tested) and Windows (builds; the sidecar window and controls are untested there).

install.release: From https://github.com/NGoochi/Alien_ID/releases, with Rhino closed: Windows, run Alien-<version>-Setup.exe (per user, no admin; SmartScreen: More info > Run anyway). It installs Alien.gha into %APPDATA%\Grasshopper\Libraries, writes settings (script folder Documents\Alien scripts, the OpenRouter key if pasted on its optional page), adds an uninstaller to Settings > Apps, and can start Rhino with Grasshopper. macOS, open Alien-<version>.pkg (Gatekeeper: System Settings > Privacy & Security > Open Anyway); it installs for the current user only and refuses while Rhino runs. Then the panel's Help (?) links OpenRouter. A by-hand zip has Alien.gha and the old scripts. Windows needs Rhino on .NET Core (SetDotNetRuntime). Full steps: installer/INSTALL.md.
requirements: .NET SDK 7 or later (building from source only)
An OpenRouter API key for describe-a-node and the AI nodes (or Ollama for local describe models)
steps_from_source: Run `dotnet build -c Release` in src/: it builds Alien.gha and copies it into Grasshopper's Libraries folder (Windows %APPDATA%\Grasshopper\Libraries; macOS ~/Library/Application Support/McNeel/Rhinoceros/8.0/Plug-ins/Grasshopper (b45a29b1-...)/Libraries). Rhino paths are in src/Alien.csproj (override with -p:RhinoSystemDir=... -p:RhinoGhDir=...).
Start Rhino and open Grasshopper: the MCP server starts with it.
Place an Alien node (tab Alien > Script). The script repository is Documents/Alien scripts unless one was chosen (right-click a node > Script repository).
Open the Alien panel, click ? (Help) and follow Connect OpenRouter; or add "openrouterKey" to settings.json (re-read live).

node.summary: One Alien node runs one script file. Saving the file (or a model or agent editing it) rebuilds the pins, keeping wires by name, and re-solves.

example: # NODE_INPUTS: base:Curve, count:int | "divisions" min=2 max=200 default=20
# Divides a curve into N points.
rules: First 200 lines; Python uses #, C# uses //. Several NODE_INPUTS / NODE_OUTPUTS lines are allowed.
Token: name:type [| "description"] [min= max= step= decimals= default= options="a|b|c" suggest="p"] [button] [image]. Commas inside quotes are fine.
Access: list[T], T[], T:list -> list; tree[T] -> tree (a list of branch lists); otherwise item.
Pin names are identities: renaming one drops its wires.
Outputs are generic; a type after : documents them.
After the pins: an optional # CATEGORY: line (a library category label), then one comment line saying what the node does (its library listing).
Python packages: # r: numpy (first 32 lines). C# references: // r "full/path.dll" or // r "nuget: Name, 1.2.3".
header.types: float int bool str Color Interval Point3d Vector3d Plane Line Circle Arc Box Rectangle3d Curve Surface Brep Mesh SubD Geometry Transform object (aliases: double/number, string/text, point, vector, domain, colour)

values: An unwired input gets, in order: its manual value (from the node's control or MCP set_values), the header default, else None / [] (C#: default(T)).
An input set to its header default holds no manual value.
Outputs are top-level variables with the output names; nested lists become data trees; tuples, sets, generators and numpy arrays become lists; Polylines become PolylineCurves.
Item-access inputs fed with lists run the script once per item.

controls.behaviour: Range from the header's min/max, else recommended from the default; a fast script (< 80 ms) follows the drag live, a slow one solves on release; double-click to type.

Momentary: true for one solve when clicked, shows 'working…' until it has run; never stored, saved or undone. For model calls and other slow, paid or side-effecting steps. set_values {name: true} presses it.
Takes an image file or link dropped on the node (its path or URL) and shows a thumbnail; typing a path or URL works too.
A list drawn under the text box follows the typing (Vicmap addresses, about 0.1 s a lookup, from the street number on); arrow keys + Enter or a click pick one.

controls.for: str, and lists of str/float/int typed as 'a, b, c'
controls.behaviour: Edited in place; the box grows with the text (up to 460 px). Enter, clicking anywhere else (another field too) or scrolling the canvas commits; Escape cancels.

runtime_controls.what: A Python script can set NODE_CONTROLS to retune its controls after a run.

fields.value: what the control shows while the input has no manual value (e.g. the built size for '0 = as built')
fields.key: what the values belong to: when a run reports a different key, values set under the old one are cleared and the node solves again

appearance: Colours from the theme (panel settings): background, text and accent, the rest mixed from them.

Header with the Alien mark (in the accent), the script name, a PY / C# badge and a state light; a status row (ok / error, run time) with a PANEL button; the error itself in a strip at the bottom; a glow when selected.
Input dots: green = wired, blue = a value set on the node or by an agent, grey = the header default.

sorting: 1. A # CATEGORY: line in the script header (matched by label or key, any case).
2. The model's pick, cached in .alien/library.json under a hash of the header (editing the header re-sorts).
3. A keyword guess (name x3, description x2, rest of header x1) until the model has answered.
Uncategorised nodes go to the model in the background, up to 40 per request, at most one request at a time and no sooner than 10 minutes after the last; only header comments are sent, never code.
Describe-a-node writes the CATEGORY line itself (the prompt lists each category's hint).

how: The request, the current script, earlier requests for the node and summaries of the wired inputs go to the model, which returns the whole file.
Alien writes it (the old version goes to .alien/history), re-solves and judges the run report: an error, unset outputs, no outputs or every output empty goes back to the model. Up to 4 attempts.
Progress shows on the node and in the panel; every request is kept in the node's transcript.

From a selection: each selected node's id, header (or component name), output summaries and one building record in full go with the request; the model answers with a 'WIRES: input <- id.output; ...' line and Alien wires the new node before its first judged run. MCP generate takes the same as context: [ids].

data_privacy_security: Describe-a-node sends the request, the current script and summaries of wired inputs to the chosen model.
The AI suite nodes send only their prompt (object_3d also the reference image given).
vic_site_map sends the address to Vicmap (Nominatim as fallback); the terrain, tree and street requests send only the map box.
Library sorting sends uncategorised scripts' header comments, not their code.
The MCP server listens on loopback only and refuses non-loopback Origins; any local process can still call it, including run_code. Don't expose the port.

Scripts run with the user's rights and can read settings.json (including the key). Read shared scripts before running them; the planned public library needs review before install and model calls routed through the plugin.

build: Rhino fully closed (pgrep Rhinoceros empty), then dotnet build -c Release in src/ (builds and deploys).
While Rhino is open: dotnet build -c Release -p:GH_Libraries= compiles without deploying.
verify: Drive it with tools/ and look at the result (capture.py, screencapture); don't claim a UI change works without seeing it.
Describe-a-node prompt or model changes: rerun tests/describe/suite.py.
Quit only a Rhino you opened: osascript -e 'tell application "Rhino 8" to quit saving no'.

conventions: Comments explain why; plain names; C# 9 / net7.0.
Header ranges and defaults are UI: give them in every node.
Suite nodes speak metres, scale to the model's units and show sample geometry when unwired.
Paid, slow or side-effecting steps go behind a button input; slider and toggle values never go into a model prompt or cache key.
Keep README, AGENTS.md, DEV_NOTES, AGENT_GUIDE and this file in step with behaviour.

nodes.name: beams_columns
nodes.listing: Beams and columns: a structural frame on the grids, columns at intersections storey by storey and beams between intersections at each level, from Australian steel, timber or concrete sections.
nodes.summary: A structural frame on the grids: columns at intersections (one member per storey) and beams from intersection to intersection at each level, in Australian steel, timber or concrete sections.
behaviour: Sections read forgivingly from alien_sections' catalogue: 193 steel sizes (UB, UC, PFC, SHS, RHS, CHS, EA, UA), glulam, LVL, sawn and concrete ('310 UB 40.4', 'SHS 150x9', '600 dia'); steel snaps to the nearest catalogue size with a note; junk falls back to the material's default.
Columns at all intersections, the perimeter or none, less a skip list ('B/2, C/3'); they turn with their grid.
Beams on both, lettered or numbered grids, top_offset below each level, stopping 12 mm off the face they meet (flange, web or flange tips); where no column stands, the continuous beams are primary.
Member records carry the exact centreline, section spec and name, level, grid and kg (info sums steel tonnes).
checked: 2026-10-13: every material, columns_at, beams_on and level option; grids rotated 15 and 30 deg (identical beam lengths); a 6x4-bay 6-storey frame (558 members) in 0.15 s.

Origin: a wired point, else the boundary's lower-left corner in project axes (anchor corner), its centroid (centre) or the world origin.

nodes.name: branch_picker
nodes.listing: Branch picker: pick one or several branches of a data tree by index ("0, 2, 4-6", "-1", "*", "even") and pass them through.
nodes.summary: Passes chosen branches of a data tree through, in the order given; the rest go out of rest.

Works by branch index: original path labels such as {0;2} are not kept.

nodes.name: connectors
nodes.listing: Connectors: base plates with anchors, cap plates, column splices, end plates, fin plates and cleats where the frame's members meet, with bolts, optional welds and a schedule.
nodes.summary: Steel connections found from the members' geometry: base plates with anchors, cap plates, column splices, end plates, fin plates and cleats, with bolts, optional welds and a schedule.

Bolt rows/columns fit the plate (or as given); edge distance and base-plate margin grow when bolts wouldn't fit.
joints records and a schedule line per joint ('BP A/1 GF: PL 505x508x25, 4 M24 anchors').

nodes.name: curtain_wall
nodes.listing: Curtain wall: mullions, transoms, perimeter frame, glass and optional back trusses along a straight, faceted or closed path, between levels.
nodes.summary: A curtain wall or glazing system along a straight, faceted, curved or closed path, between levels (or a height): mullions, transoms, frame, glass and optional trusses, with a plan cut and records.
behaviour: The exterior is on the right of an open path's direction; closed outlines face out; flip swaps.
Mullions at a panel width (equal divide, fixed from start or centred); arcs and splines are faceted into straight chords; every corner gets a mullion turned to the bisector.
Transoms at every level and/or typed heights ('1.2, 2.4', '@1.5', '-0.9' down from the top), per storey or from the wall base.
Mullion and transom profiles box, I, T, round, fin (frameless glass with 12 mm joints) or flat bar, in mm.
Optional warren, pratt, howe or vierendeel trusses behind the mullions (depth, chord and web sections).
Member counts are capped (300 mullions, 1,500 cells, 1,500 truss members) with a note.
checked: 2026-10-13: every profile pair, truss type and fit mode; line, arc, spline, circle, CW/CCW rectangles, L-shape, sloped and doubled-back paths; offsets and flip; a 48 m 12-storey wall with trusses (956 valid solids).

nodes.name: object_3d
nodes.listing: 3D object: describe a thing (or give a picture), press Generate, and a model writes RhinoCommon code that builds it from solids at real-world size.
nodes.summary: Describe a thing (or give a picture), press Generate, and a model writes RhinoCommon code that builds it from solids at real size, with part names and materials. Width, depth and height resize the built design.
behaviour: Only the generate button calls the model. Changing thing, style, image, detail or variant waits for it ('Press Generate to build ...'); nothing is sent until then.
A design built before comes back free from the cache (<repo>/.alien/cache/objects), with or without the button. The default request ('a dining chair') ships with its design.

The model (setting model3d, default anthropic/claude-sonnet-5.5) writes def build(rg, math) returning (name, material, brep) tuples in metres, Z up, standing on z = 0, front facing -Y, from robust primitives (no booleans or fillets). Alien runs it with only rg and math, checks the parts and that the size is plausible (3 cm to 8 m), and sends any error back: up to 3 attempts.

Width, depth and height never call the model: each axis scales the built design on its own; 0 or unset means as built. After a build the sliders show the design's size and span half to twice it (NODE_CONTROLS); sizes set for one design reset when the design changes.
Each design is saved once to the asset library at its built size (geometry.3dm, build.py, thumbnail, the reference image); resizing never makes a new asset.
nodes.cost: US$0.01-0.02 per design (Sonnet 5.5); free from the cache.
checked: Dining chair 18 parts 0.44 x 0.42 x 0.90 m US$0.017; dining table for six 15 parts US$0.011; toilet with cistern 14 parts US$0.015; lounge armchair from a product photo 17 parts US$0.019; bar stool US$0.013; wall basin US$0.020. All first attempt.
Resizing, re-pressing Generate on a built design and switching between built designs made no model calls and no assets.
nodes.security: The generated code runs with a restricted builtins dict and only rg and math: not a sandbox (Python introspection can escape one). It comes from the user's own model call and is shown in the code output.

nodes.name: vic_site_map
nodes.listing: Victorian site map: an address becomes the lot, neighbouring lots, roads, terrain, 3D streets, trees, building massing, zone and overlays (Vicmap, GA, Overture Maps).
nodes.summary: A Victorian address (or lat,lon) becomes a site model: the lot, neighbouring lots, road centrelines, terrain with contours, 3D streets, trees, building massing standing on the ground, and the planning zone, overlays and bushfire status.
behaviour: Geocodes with Vicmap's address index (Nominatim as fallback; a match on only the street or suburb is refused).
Lot from Vicmap Property; neighbouring lots from Vicmap Parcel; roads from Vicmap Transport.

Buildings from the Overture Maps buildings archive (PMTiles, read by HTTP range), OpenStreetMap Overpass as fallback. Height: Overture height, else storeys x 3 m + 1 m, else the tallest building part, else assumed_height.

Terrain: Geoscience Australia 5 m LiDAR DEM where it covers the site, gaps filled from the statewide Vicmap Elevation 10 m DEM; surface models (Terrarium, Open-Meteo) only if both fail. A 2 m grid, at most 201 x 201 points.

Streets: each centreline gets a cross-section from its road class, fitted to the road reserve measured from Vicmap road casement polygons (property line to property line). Carriageway, median, nature strip, footpath; lanes (reserve <= 7.5 m) wall to wall with no kerb; verges paved in central/commercial zones (CCZ, CDZ, ACZ, C1Z, MUZ, DZ, PDZ). Bands and reserves are overlaid into planar regions, classified, meshed and draped on the ground; verges sit a 150 mm kerb above the road, with kerb faces between.

Trees: Vicmap Vegetation Tree Urban points with LiDAR height and canopy half-widths, modelled by shape: broad (clumps of lumpy low-poly blobs on a split trunk with limbs), columnar, eucalypt (open high crown), conifer (stacked cones) or palm (trunk and fronds), from the species where known (City of Melbourne) else from proportions, seeded per tree. Trees under 1.5 m get a height from their canopy; points inside a building footprint reading roof height are left out.

Geometry is in metres scaled to the model's units, centred on the site, Y = true north. z = 0 is the ground at the site centre (datum gives its AHD height). Curves stay flat at z = 0 for modelling; ground, buildings, streets and trees follow the terrain.
Fetched data is cached for 30 days in the temp folder (alien-cache/vic_site_map), each v2 layer on its own; refresh (a button) fetches again once.
Data is fetched for a context bucket (60, 120, 200 or 300 m) and trimmed to the radius, so sliding the radius within a bucket refetches nothing.
The address field suggests Victorian addresses while typing (Vicmap address index, about 0.1 s per lookup).
If Vicmap's ArcGIS property/parcel layers fail (as after a republish on 12 Oct 2026), the same layers are read from the open-data WFS and info says so.
data_sources: Vicmap Address, Property, Parcel, Transport, Planning, Elevation, Vegetation (State of Victoria, CC BY 4.0)
DEM of Australia from LiDAR 5 m (Geoscience Australia, CC BY 4.0)
City of Melbourne urban forest (CC BY)
nodes.speed: First fetch for an address 2-10 s (about 35 s seen in the CBD); about 1 s from the cache; a 240 m radius with streets about 6 s from the cache.
checked: 201 Napier St Fitzroy: 4,710 m2 lot, NRZ1, HO180 + DCPO1; terrain 28.7-39.1 m AHD; 65 street centrelines (58 fitted to measured reserves); 300+ trees
Monbulk: about 35 m fall, 79 contours, streets draped on the slope
120 Collins St: CCZ1, paved verges, a grassed median, 51 trees with species for 27
limits: Not a Planning Property Report: confirm with VicPlan.
Microsoft ML building heights ran about 2.3 m low in inner Melbourne.
Tree data covers metro Melbourne, Ballarat, Shepparton, Wangaratta and Sale only.

nodes.listing: Windows: hosted windows (fixed, casement, awning, hopper, sliding, double hung) cut into walls, with frames, sashes, glass and drawing symbols.
nodes.summary: Windows hosted in wall records: fixed, casement, awning, hopper, sliding, double hung, at a sill height, cut through every layer, with frames, sashes, glass and drawing symbols.
behaviour: Hosted, placed and chained like doors; a window may sit above a door.

Plan symbols are dashed when the window is above the cut; reflected view; elevation marks show the hinge side (side-hung casement, top-hung awning, bottom-hung hopper) or arrows (sliding, double hung).
design: generated geometry is fitted into each sash.

helpers.what: Alien's settings, OpenRouter chat (with images for vision) and image generation, with caches in <repo>/.alien/cache. Requests deny data collection and report their cost.

Saves what nodes generate to <repo>/.alien/assets/<kind>/<id>/ with asset.json, geometry.3dm (metres, per-object names and colours) and a thumbnail (images fitted, or an isometric shaded render of geometry drawn with Eto).
Prompting, image model, cache, silhouette tracing and true-size placement for scale_figure and scale_tree; saves drawings as 'graphic' assets.

Victorian open data for vic_site_map: elevation_grid (GA LiDAR, Vicmap 10 m LERC tiles with a pure-Python decoder, fallbacks), trees (Tree Urban + City of Melbourne species), streets (centreline cross-sections fitted to measured reserves).

connect.claude_code: claude mcp add --transport http alien http://127.0.0.1:9876/mcp

notes: Ids are the 8-character ids from canvas/objects; a unique nickname also works for nodes.
Tool failures come back as isError results with a message, so agents can correct themselves.
Every tool that changes something returns the new state: don't poll.
mcp.server_instructions:
Alien: Grasshopper nodes backed by script files (Python 3 or C#) in the user's script repository.
Pins come from header comments ('//' instead of '#' in C#):
  # NODE_INPUTS: pts:list[Point3d], n:int | "count" min=1 max=50 default=5
  # NODE_OUTPUTS: curves, log
Unwired input -> manual value (set_values) -> header default -> None/[] (C#: default(T)). Outputs are top-level variables with those names; nested lists become data trees.
Loop: canvas -> add (python|csharp|any GH component; nodes+links for a whole chain) -> wire -> script_edit (returns ok/error+line/output summary) -> inspect / capture.
Pick Python for quick iteration and libraries; C# for heavy loops (simulations, 100k+ items) or strict typing.
Rhino side: doc (context, save, import), objects (list/select/zoom), layers (tree, visibility, materials), view (camera, display), rhino (commands, find, help). search finds GH components.
Ids are the 8-char ids from canvas/objects (a unique nickname also works for nodes). docs(topic) has syntax, types, gotchas.

tools.name: canvas
tools.description: Compact graph of the active Grasshopper document: nodes (id, type, name, state, pins; sel = selected by the user) and wires 'src.out>dst.in'.

parameters.name: filter
parameters.description: 'alien', 'errors', or a name substring. Default: everything.

parameters.name: detail
parameters.description: Include pins of native components too.

parameters.name: solve
parameters.description: Recompute the whole definition first and report errors/warnings.

tools.name: add
tools.description: Place a node. component='python'|'csharp' creates an Alien node with a new script in the repository (or attaches `script`); any other value places that Grasshopper component by name or search id (e.g. 'Number Slider', 'Panel'; 'Category:Name' when plugins share a name). Returns id, pins and (Alien) the first run report. Whole chains: `nodes` (each {key, component, name?, script?, code?, x?, y?, values?}) plus `links` ('key.out>key.in', keys or ids) in one call.

parameters.name: component
parameters.description: 'python', 'csharp', a Grasshopper component name, or an id from search

parameters.name: code
parameters.description: Initial script source (Alien). Omit for a starter template.

parameters.name: script
parameters.description: Attach an existing script instead (repo-relative or absolute path).

parameters.name: near
parameters.description: Place to the right of this node id

parameters.name: links
parameters.description: Batch: wires between the new nodes (keys) and existing ids

tools.name: wire
tools.description: Connect (or disconnect) wires. Each link is 'srcId.outputParam>dstId.inputParam'; the param part may be omitted for single-pin nodes and sliders/panels. Links that would create a loop are refused.

parameters.name: replace
parameters.description: Drop each target input's existing wires first (links in this call still accumulate)

tools.name: delete
tools.description: Remove nodes from the canvas (script files are kept).

tools.name: search
tools.description: Search the Grasshopper component library: every word must appear in a name, nickname, description or category. Returns 'Name [nick] (Category/Sub) id'; pass the id to add when names clash. detail=true (or a single hit) lists the top hit's inputs and outputs.

parameters.name: query
parameters.description: Words to match, e.g. 'curtain wall cell'

parameters.name: category
parameters.description: Restrict to a tab/category, e.g. 'VisualARQ' or 'Curve/Division'

tools.name: script_read
tools.description: Read an Alien node's script. With from/to, returns numbered lines only.

tools.name: script_edit
tools.description: Change an Alien node's script and wait for Grasshopper to re-solve. Either `edits` (exact find/replace, each `old` must match once) or full `code`. Previous version goes to .alien/history. Returns the run report.

tools.name: generate
tools.description: Describe-a-node: a model (OpenRouter, or 'ollama:<name>' locally) writes the script from plain English, runs it and fixes its own errors. Omit id for a new node; on an existing id the request edits its script. Returns attempts, cost and the run report.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Alien node to change (omit to create one)

parameters.name: context
parameters.description: Nodes the new node works with: the model sees what they output and wires them in

parameters.name: near
parameters.description: Place to the right of this node id

tools.name: inspect
tools.description: Summarise a node's data: Alien run report + input sources, or any component's outputs (counts, types, ranges, bbox, samples).

tools.name: set_values
tools.description: Set values and re-solve. Alien: manual values for unwired inputs by name (null clears). Slider: {value,min,max,decimals}. Panel: {text}. Toggle: {value}. Value List: {value: item name}. Any other component: values for its unwired inputs by nickname (arrays = several items). `preview` shows/hides viewport preview of any node(s).

parameters.name: preview
parameters.description: Show (true) or hide (false) the node's viewport preview

tools.name: run_code
tools.description: Run a throwaway Python 3 or C# snippet inside Rhino (API exploration, document queries). Returns printed output and the value of `result` if assigned.

tools.name: capture
tools.description: PNG of the Rhino viewport (default) or the Grasshopper canvas. Camera/display options are the same as `view` but apply to this capture only; the user's view is restored unless keep=true.

parameters.name: zoom
parameters.description: true/'extents', 'selected', or a box [[x,y,z],[x,y,z]] (extents is the default when `view` is given without camera/focus)

parameters.name: keep
parameters.description: Leave the viewport at the new camera/display afterwards

tools.name: view
tools.description: Set the active Rhino viewport without capturing (persistent): view preset, camera/look_at, lens, projection, display mode, zoom or focus. Returns the resulting camera.

tools.name: objects
tools.description: Rhino document objects. Filter by ids (8-char or full), layer (includes sublayers), type, name (substring), selected, hidden. action 'list' (default: counts by type/layer, bbox, first `limit` rows 'id type layer name'), 'select' (replaces the selection) or 'zoom' (frames them in the active view).

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: point, pointcloud, curve, surface, brep, extrusion, mesh, subd, block, annotation, hatch, light

tools.name: layers
tools.description: Rhino layers. Without `path`: the layer tree with object counts, flags and materials. With `path`: creates the layer if missing, then applies visible, locked, current, color, material (a document material name, a Rhino material-library search like 'Glass brick' or 'Matte Steel', or {color, transparency, gloss}).

parameters.name: filter
parameters.description: List only layers whose path contains this

parameters.name: color
parameters.description: Layer colour '#RRGGBB' or a colour name

parameters.name: material
parameters.description: Material name / library search string, or {color, transparency 0-1, gloss 0-1, name?}

tools.name: doc
tools.description: Rhino + Grasshopper documents. action 'info' (default: file, units, counts, selection, active view, GH document, versions), 'save' (both documents in place), 'save_copy' (`path`: .3dm copy or export by extension, `gh_path`: .gh copy; documents keep their own paths), 'import' (merge a file into the Rhino document), 'open_gh' (open `path`, or the editor with a blank document), 'plugins' (third-party Rhino plug-ins and Grasshopper libraries).

tools.name: rhino
tools.description: Run a Rhino command and return what it printed; without arguments, return recent command-line history. find: command names containing text. help: the command's help page from docs.mcneel.com.

parameters.name: find
parameters.description: List command names containing this, e.g. 'va' or 'array'

parameters.name: help
parameters.description: Command name to look up, e.g. 'ArrayCrv'

tools.name: bake
tools.description: Bake a node's output data into the Rhino document (anything bakeable: geometry, plugin objects). Objects are tagged; by default the node's previous bake is deleted first, so re-baking replaces instead of duplicating.

parameters.name: param
parameters.description: Output name (default: all outputs; for sliders/params: the node itself)

parameters.name: layer
parameters.description: Target layer full path, e.g. 'Model::Walls' (created if missing; default current layer)

parameters.name: replace
parameters.description: Delete this node/param's previous bake first (default true)

tools.name: docs
tools.description: Alien reference. Call with no topic for the topic list.

tools.name: repo
tools.description: Script repository: show root and scripts, or set the root folder. library=true: nodes by category with descriptions, plus generated assets.
